prediction:
THOUGHT: This patient is in the immediate postpartum period after a prolonged vaginal delivery with fever (102°F), tachycardia, and focal uterine tenderness — findings most consistent with infection of the uterine lining. Prolonged labor and macrosomic infant increase risk for ascending polymicrobial infection. Uterine tenderness is the hallmark of postpartum endometritis; foul lochia may be present (not reported here). Other diagnoses considered: urinary tract infection/pyelonephritis (urinary frequency present but no dysuria and urinalysis pending), pneumonia/atelectasis (minor bibasilar crackles but no hypoxia), retained products or ovarian vein thrombosis (less likely given presentation). Decreased bowel sounds and tympany may reflect ileus or nonspecific postoperative/postpartum GI hypomotility. Pending labs (CBC, urinalysis) will support the diagnosis but the clinical picture most strongly indicates endometritis and warrants prompt empiric broad-spectrum IV antibiotics covering anaerobes and common genital tract flora. 

DIAGNOSIS: Postpartum endometritis (acute puerperal endometritis).
